summary.text: 衣 is a whole-picture sign for an upper garment, shown with a collar, sleeves, and overlapping lapels. It commonly means clothing and is also used for “wear.”

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts an upper garment. Early forms are described as showing a collar, sleeves, and overlapping front lapels; no separate internal components are established. The Han-period explanation that it shows two covered people is a historical interpretation of the graph.

history.text: Oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal, and Shuowen forms show the graph in different script styles, but the available descriptions do not give a dated, stroke-by-stroke sequence. The curated oracle-style image is a modern redraw, and its exact specimen date is unspecified.
In the disputed 天亡簋 phrase, the graph has been read as 卒 or 殷 and given a separate ritual interpretation. These readings do not establish another meaning or a borrowing history for 衣.

uncertainties.text: The earliest dated use specifically meaning “upper garment” is unresolved: reported oracle-bone uses are mainly names, and the cited bronze garment use has no independently established date here.
Clothing, covering, coating, membrane, and other senses are recorded, but their dates and a continuous path of development are not established.

Reconstructions distinguish the clothing noun from the verb “wear” with an Old Chinese *-s contrast. This is compatible with a morphological relationship, but does not establish when the verb arose or which sense came first.

senses.text: Early graphic analyses identify the depicted object as an upper garment; the earliest dated word use with this meaning is unresolved.
衣 is used for clothing generally as well as for an upper garment.
衣 is also used as a verb meaning “wear” or “put on.” The cited examples do not date its relationship to the clothing noun.
Dictionaries record a covering or wrapping use, but do not establish when it arose or how it relates historically to the garment sense.

developments.text: The meaning may have broadened from a particular garment to clothing generally, though the change is not traced through dated stages.

limitations.text: The recorded senses do not establish a dated chain from upper garment to clothing, covering, coating, membrane, or other uses.
The reconstructed noun–verb contrast does not by itself prove derivation or its chronology.

overview.text: 衣 is a whole-picture sign for an upper garment, with a collar and overlapping sides. It commonly means clothing and is also used for “wear.”
